newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stock market fall "speculation" -- BNDES.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stock market fall "speculation" -- BNDES.

text.p: Brazil National Development Bank (BNDES) President Luiz Carlos Mendonca de Barros said this week's oscillations on the Brazilian stock market were nothing more than the result of speculation over the recent devaluations in Southeast Asia.

"This decoupling of the market's virtual reality from the real economic world has only one explanation and that is speculation," Barros said. "Important players have been taking a ride on distant events, a ride based on ignorance."

Barros, who was speaking at a press conference at the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange, said anyone who had an in-depth knowledge of Southeast Asian economies knew that recent events were specific to the region and did not apply to Brazil.
Planning Minister Antonio Kandir, who was also present at the press conference, said the government assessed the situation with calm and certainty, and concluded it would not evolve into a crisis.
"It will not develop into a crisis if the fundamentals are well positioned. The fundamentals of the Brazilian economy are well positioned," he said.
